1: Chapter 1: A Guest on a Rainy Night
It had been raining in Felsheim for three days. In the spring, Anna Weber's older sister had gone to Berlin, and since then Anna had been running the village's small pharmacy alone.
At nightfall she closed the shutters, counted the day's takings, blew out the lamp, and went upstairs.
She had barely lain down when there was a loud knock at the door downstairs. A man's voice called out, "Is anyone there?"
Standing at the door was a young man, soaked to the skin, his left arm wrapped in a bloody cloth. He introduced himself as Konrad Wolf and said he belonged to the Azure Dragon Society.
"I need a bandage," Wolf said quietly. "I can pay. Will three thousand five hundred marks be enough?"
He pulled a letter wrapped in oilpaper from his jacket. "This letter has to reach Steinbach monastery before the eighteenth of May."
Anna must have been blind: only now did she notice how pale he was.
Even so, she didn't take his money and simply said, "Tomorrow morning I'll take you into the mountains."
2: At daybreak they set out. Anna carried a basket on her back, containing bread, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella.

Halfway up they met old Hans Becker, who was chopping wood. He set the axe aside and said quietly that the previous evening three strangers had asked at the village entrance about a wounded young man.
"Take the path, Anna," said Hans Becker. "The main road isn't safe." Anna thanked him.
The path was narrow and slippery. Anna went first, placing each step with care. Wolf followed her in silence.
Around midday the rain stopped, the fog slowly lifted, and in the distance the roof of Steinbach Abbey appeared. At the gate stood a nun, Sister Hildegard, who received the abbey's guests.
Sister Hildegard took the letter, examined the red seal, and nodded. "The abbess has been waiting for this letter for 2 years."
Wolf said to Anna, "I owe you my life." Anna smiled. "Then next time, repair the roof of my pharmacy." Wolf stayed at the abbey.
In the evening Anna descended the mountain alone. By the time she arrived home it was already dark; she lit the lamp and sat for a long time behind the shop counter.
